records.description: The height of the cone falls at a constant rate, and the radius, the height, and the radius rate are known at a stated time. The part asks for the rate of change of the volume at that time, so the supplied cone volume formula must be differentiated with respect to time, treating both the radius and the height as functions of time, and the given values substituted.
records.anchor_quote: The height of the cone decreases at a rate of 2 centimeters per day
scoring_behaviors: The scoring guidelines for this year number the points within each part, such as the first point and the second point of the part, rather than running from P1 to P9 across the whole question (sg-22:16).
First point: a complete product rule across the two varying quantities earns it, and it is lost when one of them is treated as constant (sg-22:16).
Second point: the chain rule factors, the two time derivatives, earn it, and a correct product rule with those factors missing earns only the first point (sg-22:16).

Third point: the evaluated answer earns it, requires both earlier points, and is unavailable when the constant factor of the volume formula is mishandled; assuming a fixed relation between the radius and the height caps the response at the chain rule point (sg-22:16).
records.notation_requirements: Leibniz notation with both time derivatives visible; the radius rate taken from the table at the stated time.
records.justification_requirements: None required.
records.difficulty_notes: Four concepts combined, a product of two varying quantities inside a supplied formula, a needed rate read from the table, no calculator, three points with a strict final dependency, and a tempting similar-triangles assumption that is penalised.
diagnostic_distinctions: one quantity held constant: the product rule structure was not recognised
product rule written without the time derivatives: the chain rule layer is missing
a proportional relation between radius and height assumed: an unstated modelling assumption replaced the given data

records.name: 2022 BC Q6(a): interval of convergence of a power series by the ratio test
records.description: A function is defined by an alternating power series with odd powers and odd denominators. The part asks for the interval of convergence by the ratio test, with justification, so the ratio of consecutive terms must be formed, the limit taken to find the interior, both endpoint series produced, and each tested.
records.anchor_quote: Using the ratio test, find the interval of convergence of the power series
scoring_behaviors: The scoring guidelines for this year number the points within each part, such as the first point and the second point of the part, rather than running from P1 to P9 across the whole question (sg-22:20).
First point: a correct ratio, with or without absolute values, earns it (sg-22:21).

Second point: the absolute value of the ratio, or an equivalent resolution, the limit evaluated with correct limit notation, and the interior named as a two sided inequality or interval, are all required; a one sided statement is insufficient (sg-22:21).
Third point: considering both endpoints earns it, and the only wrong interior that stays eligible is the one running from zero to one, in which case one endpoint suffices (sg-22:21).
Fourth point: the endpoint analysis with the named test and the stated interval earns it, and a substitution error in the exponent forfeits only this point (sg-22:21).
records.notation_requirements: Ratio with the index advanced throughout, absolute values, limit notation, and the interval written with correct endpoint inclusion.
records.justification_requirements: Each endpoint series must be tested by a named test before the interval is stated.
records.difficulty_notes: Three concepts combined, four sequential rubric points, index and exponent bookkeeping, endpoint work that is a separate subproblem, no calculator, notation scored at every step.
diagnostic_distinctions: interior found but endpoints untested: the interval is left open where the work was incomplete
exponent substitution wrong in the advanced term: index bookkeeping, not the test, failed
limit stated without limit notation: communication, not convergence reasoning, failed
